integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: thermal release during start-up after maintenance on TX-7001

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage.

defences.finding: Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an organisational factor.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the ICAM investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Restore the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on TX-7001 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in managing hydrocarbon transfer and storage, specifically transferring hydrocarbon between vessels. TX-7001 (terminal switchgear) is in service for terminal distribution. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 5 January 2016 an incident occurred on TX-7001 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during start-up after maintenance, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
